categories.label: Traditional Delivery Method Limitations for MMC
categories.memo: Covers evidence and reasoning as to why conventional design-bid-build and similarly fragmented delivery methods are structurally mismatched to the needs of modular/off-site/prefabricated construction, primarily due to late contractor and supplier involvement and rigid risk allocation.

codes.label: Late involvement of manufacturer/contractor under DBB
codes.description: DBB sequences design completion before contractor/manufacturer selection, preventing early input needed for modular/prefab buildability and coordination.

codes.label: Fragmentation and adversarial relationships
codes.description: Traditional contract forms create vertical, horizontal and longitudinal fragmentation among stakeholders, hindering the collaboration DfMA/MMC requires.

codes.label: Rigid risk allocation unsuited to complex projects
codes.description: Traditional delivery/contract structures allocate risk and responsibility rigidly among parties, producing suboptimal outcomes for complex, innovative construction methods.

codes.label: Design freeze and change sensitivity
codes.description: Modular/prefab production requires early design freeze; late changes under traditional sequencing severely disrupt fabrication, transportation and installation.

codes.label: Unfamiliarity and industry distrust
codes.description: Parties unfamiliar with modular/prefab procedures and traditional adversarial industry culture create elevated risk of project problems under conventional delivery.

categories.label: Integrated and Collaborative Delivery Models
categories.memo: Encompasses delivery methods and contractual frameworks (IPD, DB, CM, ECI, partnering) that integrate design, procurement and construction to better support MMC/prefabrication, including their defining features and comparative performance.

codes.label: Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) suitability
codes.description: IPD's multiparty agreements, shared risk/reward and early involvement of all parties are identified as well matched to modular/precast and DfMA requirements.

codes.label: Design-Build as an integration mechanism
codes.description: Design-Build combines design and construction responsibility under one party, offering single-point responsibility, greater contractual integration, and better performance metrics than DBB for innovative projects.

codes.label: Construction Management (CM) delivery
codes.description: CM/CM-GC delivery is recommended for complex prefabrication projects, allowing pricing flexibility and easier incorporation of contractor innovations such as ATCs.

codes.label: Early Contractor/Manufacturer Involvement (ECI) mechanisms
codes.description: Two-stage tendering, ECI, and pre-construction service agreements enable contractor/manufacturer buildability input before design lock, balancing collaboration with price certainty.

sub_codes.label: Payment models for pre-construction services
sub_codes.description: Various models (unpaid, reimbursed if not proceeding, discounted) for compensating contractor involvement during pre-construction design phase.

codes.label: Partnering, alliancing and relational contracting
codes.description: Strategic partnering, alliancing and relational contract models create shared pain/gain arrangements and collaborative culture that support MMC/OSC implementation.

codes.label: Vertically integrated and manufacturer-led models
codes.description: New contractual entities combining manufacturing with builder/design-builder roles, or fully vertically integrated firms, increase team integration beyond conventional procurement systems.

categories.label: Delivery Method Selection, Feasibility and Comparative Assessment
categories.memo: Concerns tools, frameworks and criteria for selecting an appropriate delivery method for MMC/off-site projects, including feasibility scoring, bundled project considerations, and the state of research gaps in this area.

codes.label: PDM feasibility and selection frameworks
codes.description: Proposed frameworks and criteria for matching project/client characteristics to delivery method characteristics, including quantitative feasibility scoring tools.

codes.label: Bundled project delivery considerations
codes.description: Delivery method selection for bundled (multi-project) contracts introduces additional risks (mutual dependence, cross-site coordination) not present in single-project delivery, affecting DBB vs DB suitability.

codes.label: Product-based vs project-based delivery paradigms
codes.description: Modular construction reflects a shift toward product-based development requiring new 'Product Delivery Models' or framework/serial contracts rather than one-off project contracts.

codes.label: Research gap on best delivery method for MiC/DfMA
codes.description: Literature has not established which project delivery method best facilitates early involvement, design liability sharing, or contractual synergy with DfMA/MiC.

codes.label: Administrative and coordination burden under MMC delivery
codes.description: Prefabrication increases planning, scheduling and coordination responsibilities, which may require delegation to a construction manager rather than remaining with designers.

categories.label: Standard Form Contract Fit and Adaptation for MMC/OSC
categories.memo: Addresses the extent to which existing standard forms (JCT, FIDIC, NEC, CCDC, AIA, ConsensusDocs) are suited to MMC/OSC delivery, and what adaptations or new contract models are needed.

codes.label: Standard form familiarity vs. misalignment
codes.description: Standard forms provide familiarity and can overcome cultural resistance, but they are also criticized as designed for traditional construction and misaligned with MMC/DfMA needs.

codes.label: Comparison of IPD standard forms (AIA C-191, ConsensusDocs 300, CCDC30)
codes.description: Different IPD standard forms vary in prescriptiveness on risk assessment, termination rights, insurance and data-sharing requirements, affecting suitability for MMC/DfMA projects.

codes.label: Payment and financial term adaptation for off-site work
codes.description: Traditional payment mechanisms (progress payments tied to on-site work, retention, liquidated damages) are unsuited to off-site manufacturing funding needs and require contractual amendment.

codes.label: Need for new/bespoke contractual frameworks
codes.description: Calls for new contract models (e.g., product delivery contracts, standardized ECI pre-construction agreements) tailored specifically to MMC/OSC rather than adapted traditional forms.
